reasoning: Plan A is the superior training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates dedicated threshold work and tempo runs, which are crucial for increasing running economy and lactate threshold – key determinants of speed. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost exclusively on easy, low-volume trail runs, which will likely lead to a plateau in performance without introducing any significant physiological challenge. While Plan B prioritizes recovery and maintaining freshness, it lacks the targeted intensity needed for genuine speed development. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training and cross-training also addresses common weaknesses in trail runners, improving stability and reducing injury risk.
